environment.working_tree: Modified worktree (50 paths): Products planning/evidence, Catalog adapter/tests and local migrations; no Supabase remote writes or migration applications.

decisions.summary: The ERP target is SMEs across sectors; this is not approval for a full ERP or every candidate module in the first release.
Prioritize MiauCraft with Shopify retained as its sales channel; Inhand follows with native LoopDev commerce.
Suppliers is a standalone ERP module, separate from Procurement; its priority and delivery date remain open. Manufacturing is deferred to future discovery.
Products is the user-facing ERP module and direct product/service list entry point; preserve catalog-named contracts, IDs, permissions and routes as compatibility until separately migrated.

Products has one master for finished products, raw materials/components and services; the product base has a general category and each separately managed/sold SKU has its own category; drafts may omit category but activation requires it; item class is independent from purchasing, selling and inventory tracking; finished products allow buy/make/both sourcing, raw materials/components are buy-only for now, services have no sourcing, and variants inherit product sourcing; semimanufactured items await Manufacturing discovery.
The product base has a general category and each variant/SKU has an independently assigned category; only sourcing is inherited from the product.
The first release is Products and categories only on desktop web and mobile web; other ERP modules and integrations remain deferred.
MiauCraft's Shopify data ownership, sync direction and allowed writes require client confirmation.
Inhand jurisdiction, tax, shipping, returns and stock reservation policies remain open.
Native iOS and Android are deferred; desktop web and mobile web are required in this release.
Catalog documentation and remote adapter/migration evidence conflict; remote runtime is unverified.
Catalog mutations use catalog.write; purchase costs use separate catalog.cost.read and catalog.cost.manage permissions, with implementation and deployed RLS parity still open.

actions: Drafted the 15-section cross-sector ERP functional/product design with explicit candidate scope and excluded enterprise capabilities.
Defined candidate context boundaries, Platform reuse decisions, interaction matrix and route status without claiming proposed paths are implemented.
Recorded the user-confirmed Suppliers module boundary, kept its release priority open, and deferred Manufacturing to future discovery.

Applied approved change request CR-ERP-PRODUCTS-MODULE across the design: Products replaces Catalog as the visible module and opens directly to the product/service list; no production route or data migration was made.

Applied user-approved CR-ERP-PRODUCT-MASTER-MODEL across discovery, design, architecture, ledger and visual scope; the category-inheritance assumption was later resolved by the user in favor of independently assigned SKU categories.
Recorded provisional lifecycle, entity, API, RBAC and local-first direction for later specialized phases.
Linked accepted market sources and documented security, multiplatform and platform-reuse dependencies.

Revalidated the design against current route and adapter source: /app/erp/products is registered, legacy catalog routing remains compatible, and catalog loading fails closed while VITE_CATALOG_ADAPTER_MODE is unset.
Updated the approved append-only audit contract status: semantics are confirmed; Products call sites, same-transaction rollback, and failure tests remain implementation gates.
Corrected architecture and platform evidence that still described ID-shape adapter selection, unimplemented routes, pending audit-owner assignment, and unimplemented mode handling.
No product scope or visual composition changed. The Product Owner reapproved current design and visual artifacts after the changed-input invalidation.
Prior specialized checkpoints 02-domain through 05-sync were invalidated by the refreshed design fingerprint and must be revalidated after the visual handoff.

validation.evidence: The approved Products/categories/cost scope remains unchanged; verified route registration, explicit fail-closed adapter mode, approved audit semantics and remaining runtime/security gates are reconciled without expanding scope.
No whitespace errors in the revalidated design and platform evidence.

requirements.evidence: Design records Suppliers as an independent ERP context and Manufacturing as deferred; first-release modules, supplier scope and sequence remain open.

Products is the visible foundation; REQ-ERP-CATALOG-FOUNDATION and CAP-ERP-CATALOG retain stable IDs; the user-confirmed master model is documented as conceptual only, while legacy contracts remain compatible and remote-runtime/permission mismatches still block implementation expansion.
Category management is included within Products as an approved requirement; current categoryKey is not a hierarchical category contract, and desktop/mobile operations remain unimplemented.
MiauCraft is prioritized and Shopify remains its channel; client field ownership and sync operations remain open.
Inhand remains a later native-commerce case; jurisdiction and operational policies remain open.
